status_reasoning: Reviewers request detailed discussion of the protein microarray approach and ask for 'estimations about false positive or false negative hits in their screening.' While the manuscript acknowledges ~27% false positive rate (C32, C84) and some false negatives (C85), reviewers express concern about the reliability of the screening method, indicating uncertainty about the breadth and accuracy of the methylated DNA-binding TF identification.

The reviewers do not challenge the finding that some TFs exhibit dual-specificity binding to methylated and unmethylated DNA motifs of distinct sequences. The identification of 17 dual-specificity TFs and the demonstration that they recognize different consensus sequences is accepted without critique.

Reviewers note that 'Figure 2F lacks negative controls' and request experiments showing 'what happens when adding both methylated and un-methylated competitor DNA' which 'should abolish KLF4 and TFAP2A binding.' This indicates the evidence for KLF4 using two different domains is incomplete and requires additional controls to be convincing.

Reviewers request that 'for a couple of transcription factor-meCpG interactions, it would be important to determine the KD of the interaction using conventional biochemistry and compare these KDs to other published meCpG-protein affinities.' While KD values are provided, reviewers indicate more comprehensive biochemical characterization and comparison to published affinities is needed to fully validate the binding strengths.

Reviewers state 'it would be important to dissect which domain or which KLF4 zinc finger is specifically mediating the interaction with un-methylated DNA.' While the manuscript shows mutations that decouple mCpG and CpG binding, reviewers indicate the mechanistic understanding of which specific domain mediates unmethylated DNA binding is insufficient and requires further dissection.

The luciferase assay data demonstrating KLF4's methylation-dependent and mutation-sensitive transcriptional activation is not challenged by reviewers. The functional validation in heterologous cells showing that mutations abolish methylated DNA-dependent activity while preserving unmethylated DNA activity is accepted without critique.

Reviewers express major concern that 'the manuscript was not successful in convincing us of the physiological relevance of the findings; specifically, the ChIP experiments must be improved.' They specifically note 'the poor quality (or presentation) of the ChIP-seq data in Figure 4A' and request 'ChIP-qPCR data for this experiment should be presented here to convince the reader that KLF4 is actually bound to these sites in vivo.' The reviewers state authors 'should better demonstrate that the dual preference of KLF4 in vivo before this work could be published,' indicating the in vivo evidence is currently insufficient.

Reviewers ask 'why were ZNF114 and ZNF416 not picked up in previous interactions screenings?' This question indicates reviewers want better contextualization and validation of these novel findings, expressing some uncertainty about why these proteins were uniquely identified in this study but not in prior work.

Reviewers request that 'authors should discuss their results in the context of previously published literature and discuss any overlap, discrepancies, and novelties' and specifically ask 'why did the authors not identify meCpG dependent interactions for Rfx proteins?' This indicates reviewers find the comparison to prior studies incomplete and want better explanation of discrepancies, suggesting uncertainty about how the findings relate to existing literature.
